variants.cost: Exactly one arm pull and one selected reward observation per round, T of each. For a direct implementation: K weights of storage, O(K) arithmetic to form and sample probabilities per round, and O(K) initialization per restart; these implementation counts follow the displayed operations and are separately charged, not a source runtime Theorem. No additional reward queries at restart.
variants.name: Rexp3 with known variation budget
variants.output: The online sequence I_1,...,I_T and its received rewards. No final best-arm recommendation or simple-regret guarantee is specified.
public_inputs: Positive integer batch size Delta and exploration parameter 0<gamma<=1
For the paper's Theorem 2 tuning: known positive V_T
variants.query_and_update: At t compute p_t^k=(1−gamma)w_t^k/(sum_l w_t^l)+gamma/K for each k. Draw I_t from this categorical distribution and observe X_t^{I_t}. Set hatX_t^k=X_t^{I_t}/p_t^{I_t} if k=I_t, and zero otherwise. Update every weight by w_{t+1}^k=w_t^k exp(gamma hatX_t^k/K). At batch end increment j and reset before the next batch.
variants.requirements: Select one arm at each round and observe only its reward in [0,1]. Fixed batches and supplied gamma define the operations. The variation-budget stochastic model is needed for the separately reported performance claim, not to execute the update.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set j=1. Batch j starts at tau=(j−1)Delta and contains t=tau+1,...,min(T,tau+Delta). At each batch start initialize all K current weights w_{tau+1}^k=1. Discard previous-batch weights.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Theorem 2 specifies Delta=ceil((K log K)^(1/3)(T/V_T)^(2/3)) and gamma=min{1,sqrt(K log K/((e−1)Delta))}, with natural log. Execute j=1,...,ceil(T/Delta), stopping after exactly T rounds. A final batch may be shorter; Delta>T yields one truncated batch. These formulas are transcribed tuning, not a newly certified performance guarantee.
